claims.text: Systematic variation of elemental composition, including substitutional doping, can be used to tune the magnetic and magnetocaloric behavior of non-equiatomic HEAs.
Changing elemental composition modifies magnetic exchange interactions.
Composition-induced changes in magnetic exchange interactions shift the magnetic transition temperature.
The baseline non-equiatomic HEA has a modest magnetocaloric response and a characteristic magnetic transition.
The proposed intervention is partial substitution of one or more elements or alteration of their relative fractions while remaining in a single-phase region.
Controlled synthesis may use arc melting followed by annealing.
Compositional adjustment modifies the local atomic environment.
Compositional adjustment produces subtle variations in solid-solution phase stability.
Altering elemental ratios changes magnetic anisotropy.
More favorable magnetostructural coupling enhances the magnetocaloric effect.
The modified alloy will exhibit a shifted magnetic transition temperature relative to the baseline composition.
The modified alloy will exhibit a broader or enhanced entropy change relative to the baseline composition.
The tuning effect is expected to persist only while the alloy remains in the single-phase solid-solution regime.
Compositions outside the single-phase range may undergo phase segregation.
Phase segregation may negate the claimed benefits of compositional tuning.
The magnitude of the transition-temperature shift and magnetocaloric improvement depends on the selected elements and their relative percentages.
